title: Performance: optimize queries + caching for Usage Insights “Top routes” view; load test + acceptance thresholds
creator: Logan Wright
project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)
body:
Context
- This issue is focused on end-to-end performance for the Usage Insights console “Top routes” view (route list + filters + pagination), which is powered by the Insights API route-list endpoint.
- We need predictable latency and bounded query costs under realistic tenant sizes + UI refresh patterns (including multiple users looking at the same org/project/time range).

Problem statement
- Current staging measurements (2026-02-20 load test) show p95 API latency ~1.6–2.1s for common queries (7d window, org+project scope, sort by total_cost) and occasional timeouts at higher concurrency.
- Primary contributors:
  1) scanning too many partitions/columns for long windows
  2) latency/p95 blowups when route cardinality is high and we compute multiple breakdowns in the same request
  3) no response caching; console refresh + filter tweaks multiply load

Goals
- Make the route list endpoint consistently fast enough for interactive console use.
- Put hard guardrails around query cost (DB time + rows scanned) to protect the analytics cluster.
- Establish a repeatable load testing plan and define acceptance thresholds for GA gate.

Non-goals
- Export job performance (tracked in ENG-8425 / export benchmarks doc).
- Anomaly detection/alerting logic beyond basic “change vs prior period” (product non-goal).

Proposed approach
A) Query plan improvements (DB-side)
1) Time-window aware source selection
- <= 48h: read from hourly aggregates only
- > 48h: read from daily aggregates only
- Note: UI currently defaults to 7d; daily should be the hot path.

2) Tighten projections / select fewer columns
- Route list endpoint should NOT fetch model breakdown by default (only on route detail).
- Remove any unused columns from SELECT to reduce IO.

3) Partitioning + ordering alignment
- Ensure tables are partitioned on (org_id, project_id, bucket_start) and ordered by (org_id, project_id, bucket_start, route_norm_hash).
- Confirm filter pushdown is happening for org_id/project_id/region/deployment_mode.

4) Avoid expensive distinct/quantile computations on the hot path
- Use precomputed rollups for token totals + cost totals.
- For latency p50/p95 in route list: use stored t-digest / histogram aggregates (if available in existing pipeline), otherwise omit latency percentiles from the list view and keep them for route detail.

5) Pagination strategy
- Prefer keyset pagination when sorting by total_cost (descending) where feasible.
- If we must keep offset pagination for v1, set a hard maximum offset (e.g., 10k) and return a clear error.

B) API caching (service-side)
1) Response cache
- Cache route list responses keyed by:
  - org_id, project_id
  - time_range (start/end rounded to minute)
  - filters (env, region, deployment_mode)
  - sort + page (or keyset cursor)
- Default TTL: 60s.
- For “Last 1h” range: TTL 10–15s.
- Implement stale-while-revalidate to prevent thundering herds when many users load the same default view.

2) Cache bypass
- Allow internal header for debugging (e.g., x-redwood-cache-bypass: true) restricted to employees/admin.

3) Observability for cache
- Emit metrics: hit_rate, evictions, key cardinality, p95 cache get time, and “served stale” counts.

C) Console behavior (light touch, no UI redesign)
- Confirm polling/auto-refresh behavior is reasonable (no more frequent than every 60s on the route list by default).
- Ensure filter changes debounce requests (Design/Console team alignment needed; tracked as part of ENG-8426 follow-ups).

Implementation notes / likely code touchpoints
- Insights API service (route list handler)
- Query builder for aggregates
- Caching layer (Redis/memcache depending on existing console backend pattern)
- DB migrations/index changes where applicable

Acceptance thresholds (GA gate)
- Environment: staging perf cluster with production-like dataset (see Load Test Plan).

API latency (route list endpoint)
- Cached responses (steady-state, default 7d view):
  - p95 <= 350ms
  - p99 <= 800ms
- Uncached responses (cold cache, default 7d view):
  - p95 <= 900ms
  - p99 <= 1500ms

DB query budget (measured at service, excluding network)
- p95 DB time <= 500ms for uncached default queries.
- No single query > 2s without being flagged (log + metric).

Error rates
- 5xx rate <= 0.5% at target QPS.
- Timeouts <= 0.1% at target QPS.

Capacity targets (initial)
- Sustain 150 RPS to route list endpoint per region (mixed tenants) with <75% CPU on API pods and without causing sustained analytics cluster queueing.
- Note: These targets are for beta/GA ramp; revisit after design partners.

Load testing plan
Tooling
- k6 scenario tests (preferred) or Locust if we need more complex per-tenant session behavior.

Datasets
- Use synthetic aggregates approximating realistic limits:
  - ~50–200 routes per project (typical)
  - Include a “stress tenant” with ~5k routes to validate guardrails/limits
  - Mix of 3 regions, 2 deployment modes
- Include enough history to test 24h, 7d, 30d windows.

Scenarios
1) Baseline interactive
- 50 RPS sustained
- 80% default 7d view, 15% filter tweaks (region/env), 5% pagination

2) Burst + cache effectiveness
- Ramp 0 -> 200 RPS over 2 minutes, hold 5 minutes
- Measure cache hit rate and tail latency under burst

3) Cold cache
- Flush cache before run; run 100 RPS for 5 minutes
- Validate uncached thresholds + DB stability

4) Stress tenant
- 20 RPS focused on the stress tenant’s project, default 7d view
- Validate hard limits (page size, max offset) and that latency degrades gracefully (no timeouts)

Instrumentation required for the tests
- Per-request: cache_hit/miss, db_time_ms, rows_scanned/bytes_read if available from DB driver, response_size
- Cluster: queue depth / query concurrency, CPU, memory

Work items
- [ ] Audit current route list query plan; capture “before” metrics and an EXPLAIN
- [ ] Implement time-window aware source selection (hourly vs daily)
- [ ] Reduce columns + remove accidental joins / extra aggregations
- [ ] Add pagination limits + clear error messaging for excessive offsets
- [ ] Implement response caching + SWR
- [ ] Add cache + DB timing metrics; wire to dashboards (ENG-8430)
- [ ] Build k6 test suite + document how to run it
- [ ] Run staged load tests and publish results in ticket comments
- [ ] Decide if latency percentiles must appear in route list for GA; if not, confirm with PM/Design

Open questions
- Do we require latency p50/p95 on the route list for GA, or can we keep that detail-only? (This materially changes query cost.)
- What is our hard cap for routes returned across all pages? (Proposal: 10k max offset or keyset-only after page N.)
- Should cache keys round start/end times (minute) to increase reuse? (Proposal: yes; document behavior.)

References
- API contract addendum: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-analytics-api-contract.json
- Engineering epic: ENG-8421
- Route list endpoint: ENG-8423
- Aggregates: ENG-8422
- Observability dashboards: ENG-8430
- Related PRs (in flight): PRs for route list endpoint + aggregates (see PR-15455, PR-15441) — this ticket may land as follow-up PR(s) once the baseline endpoint is stable.
comments: 2026-02-12 (Logan Wright): Flagging as P1 for GA gating. We need clear thresholds + a load test harness before we expand beta beyond design partners.

2026-02-20 (Jada Williams): Ran quick k6 smoke against staging with ~40 RPS; p95 ~1.8s on 7d default. DB time dominates; no caching currently. Next step: split hourly vs daily source and remove latency percentile calcs from list view (keep for route detail).

2026-02-22 (Allison Grant): Please add explicit metrics for db_time_ms and cache_hit, and wire alerts for p95 regression. Also add a circuit breaker / query timeout (server-side) so we fail fast rather than pile up on the analytics cluster.
